modules.name: Cross-Functional Alignment
modules.framework: McKinsey 7S — systems and staff across BD and operations

findings.Red: Sales sells what operations cannot staff. Handoffs fail.
findings.Yellow: Forums exist; one capacity plan does not.
findings.Green: BD and ops share one plan, one promise, one backlog.

findings.Red: Cadence and decision rights do not convert strategy into weekly work.
findings.Yellow: Leaders meet; they do not decide with owners and dates.
findings.Green: A visible operating rhythm holds people to commitments.

findings.Red: Initiatives spawn without a tracker, owner, or done-definition.
findings.Yellow: Work is tracked; red items do not get resources.
findings.Green: A lightweight TO keeps the stack honest.

modules.name: Operating Model Redesign
modules.framework: McKinsey / Deloitte operating model — process, structure, governance

findings.Red: Cost-to-serve and bottlenecks are the business model.
findings.Yellow: The constraint is known; it is not subordinated.
findings.Green: Throughput, cost, and commitment sit on one design.

modules.name: Culture and Incentives
modules.framework: McKinsey Influence Model — role modeling, reinforcement

findings.Red: Commission pays for sold work that destroys margin or delivery.
findings.Yellow: Incentives are mixed; delivery has no score.

modules.name: Governance Cadence
modules.framework: McKinsey 7S — superordinate goals and weekly operating review

findings.Red: No weekly operating review. Strategy lives in decks.
findings.Yellow: Meetings happen; they do not produce decisions.
findings.Green: Weekly ops, monthly strategy, quarterly capital.

modules.name: Cost and Throughput Excellence
modules.framework: Deloitte Enterprise Value Map / lean constraint

findings.Red: Costs rise with complexity; rework is hidden capacity.
findings.Yellow: Cost-to-serve is visible; it is not redesigned.
findings.Green: Constraint and CTS are managed as operating levers.

findings.Red: The strategy requires seats the org does not have.
findings.Yellow: Skills exist in heroes, not in the system.
findings.Green: Critical seats and standard work can carry the model.

archetypes.name: Operating Model Broken
archetypes.headline: BD and operations are two companies. Growth will move the bottleneck, not remove it.
archetypes.situation: Handoffs, cost-to-serve, and leadership cadence cannot support the commercial promise.
archetypes.implication: More pipeline without one plan will raise overtime, rework, and margin leakage.
archetypes.recommendation: One capacity plan, one handoff standard, one weekly forum, incentive realignment.
rootCause: Sales and delivery do not share a capacity truth
Estimating and scope control are the hidden factory
Leadership cadence is too weak to hold commitments
Incentives pay for sold work, not delivered contribution

archetypes.name: Alignment Strained
archetypes.headline: The operating model almost works — until volume, mix, or a tough job hits.
archetypes.situation: Forums and good intent exist. Decision rights, CTS, and incentives still leak.
archetypes.implication: You will keep fighting the same fires every quarter.
archetypes.recommendation: Codify RACI, visual constraint, and a sell-and-deliver score.
rootCause: Cross-functional alignment is personal, not systemic
Cost-to-serve is not an owned lever
Governance produces discussion more than decisions

archetypes.name: Aligned Execution
archetypes.headline: The operating model can carry growth. Protect it as you scale.
archetypes.situation: Cadence, handoffs, and cost discipline are in a healthy band.
archetypes.implication: The risk is initiative overload and incentive drift, not a broken core.
archetypes.recommendation: Keep one KPI stack. Add seats before adding promises.
rootCause: BD and ops can share one plan
Scale requires capability, not a new philosophy

initiatives.name: One Plan: Capacity vs Commitment
initiatives.summary: Publish a weekly capacity vs. backlog view. Sales cannot sell what ops cannot staff.

initiatives.name: Commercial-to-Delivery Handoff Standard
initiatives.summary: A deal is not won until scope, margin, and date survive a joint review.

initiatives.name: Estimating SLA and Truth Book
initiatives.summary: Time-box estimating, version it, and feed actuals back into the book.

initiatives.name: Weekly BD–Ops Alignment Forum
initiatives.summary: 45 minutes: at-risk jobs, oversold capacity, next-week commitments.

initiatives.name: Delivery Promise System
initiatives.summary: Only dates operations has signed can appear in proposals.

initiatives.name: Incentive Alignment (Sell and Deliver)
initiatives.summary: Do not pay full commission on jobs that destroy margin or delivery.

initiatives.name: Visual Management of the Constraint
initiatives.summary: Make the bottleneck visible to sellers and floor leaders from the same board.

initiatives.name: Scope Control and Change Orders
initiatives.summary: Unpriced scope is the silent margin killer.

initiatives.name: Cost-to-Serve Reduction Program
initiatives.summary: Separate high-cost customers and job types. Redesign service or reprice.

initiatives.name: Constraint Mapping (TOC)
initiatives.summary: Find the one constraint that sets throughput. Subordinate everything else.

initiatives.name: Rework and First-Time-Right
initiatives.summary: Rework is hidden capacity. Measure it, then redesign the handoff that causes it.

initiatives.name: Leadership Cadence Reset
initiatives.summary: Weekly operating review, monthly strategy, quarterly capital. Decision rights written down.

initiatives.name: Three-Priority Rule
initiatives.summary: Leadership may run three enterprise priorities. Everything else is a project.

initiatives.name: Decision Rights (RACI) for Commercial and Ops
initiatives.summary: Who can commit a date, a price, and a scope.

initiatives.name: Lightweight Transformation Office
initiatives.summary: One tracker, one owner, biweekly red/yellow/green on the initiative stack.

initiatives.name: One KPI Stack Across BD and Ops
initiatives.summary: Five enterprise KPIs. Separate scoreboards make alignment theater.

initiatives.name: Standard Work on the Critical Path
initiatives.summary: Document and coach the few processes that actually move throughput.

initiatives.name: 13-Week Cash and Booking Bridge
initiatives.summary: Stabilize first: bookings, billings, cash. Growth talk waits until the bridge is honest.
